newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodians protest at site of deadly attack.
newsitem.headline: Cambodians protest at site of deadly attack.

text.p: About 10 students protested in front of Cambodia's parliament on Tuesday, the first time demonstrators have ventured on to the site since a deadly March grenade attack there.

The sight of students holding placards stopped traffic and curious pedestrians, who watched the young men and women stand quietly at the site where unknown assailants lobbed four grenades at a March 30 opposition rally.

The attack, an apparent attempt to assassinate opposition leader Sam Rainsy, killed up to 19 people, wounded more than 150 and effectively stopped Cambodian demonstrators from taking to the streets for weeks.
Fresh flowers lay at the spot where one of the grenades exploded.

Tuesday's protesters, who included the students' teacher, said they wanted to express anger over what they said was their illegal detention by police over the weekend in a dispute over alleged threats to another student.
A human rights worker said the student protesters spent two days and nights in jail in Phnom Penh without being charged and now wanted compensation and a guarantee of their safety.
The protest was the first test of the Cambodian government's stance toward demonstrations since the grenade attack.

Cambodian leaders have sent mixed messages since March 30, with one Interior Minister announcing a temporary ban on demonstrations but other officials saying protests would be approved on a case-by-case basis.
A handful of unarmed Interior Ministry police said they had no problem with the demonstration, which proceeded peacefully.
Rights officials have expressed fears that violence could result from future demonstrations and some doubt that those behind the March attack will be brought to justice.
However Interior Ministry officials say an investigation is under way and U.S. FBI (Federal Bureau of Investigation) agents have completed sketches of possible suspects.
